lines.text: Hollywood rented most of its jewels.
Eugene Joseff urged studios to use jewelry from the right era.
Studios rented his pieces instead of buying them.
His special gold finish cut the glare of studio lights.
Vivien Leigh's jewelry in Gone with the Wind was his.
So was Rhett Butler's cigar case.
Elizabeth Taylor's jewelry in Cleopatra came from him too.
Marilyn Monroe wore his pieces in Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.
His pieces later appeared on television shows too.
His widow, Joan Castle Joseff, ran the company until 2010.

post.caption: Hollywood rented most of its jewels. Eugene Joseff urged studios to use jewelry from the right era, and they rented his pieces instead of buying them. His gold finish cut the glare of studio lights. Vivien Leigh's jewelry in Gone with the Wind was his, and so was Rhett Butler's cigar case. Elizabeth Taylor's jewelry in Cleopatra came from him too, and Marilyn Monroe wore his pieces in Gentlemen Prefer Blondes. His widow, Joan Castle Joseff, ran the company until 2010. His firm supplied an estimated ninety percent of film jewelry.
